tasks.short: Train people to use computer systems

steps.what: Prepare the computer system practice sheet

loop.input: topic list and the sheet template
loop.output: a sheet that cites topic ids only
loop.check: Every exercise cites a topic id on the list
loop.stop: One pass, then drop any exercise with no topic id
loop.why_not_simpler: How to explain a mistake in the room is not a fixed script

steps.what: Train people in computer system use
Practice the computer system skill
Record the people the administrator will train

tasks.design: A bounded note in {DOCS} prepares a practice sheet for the computer system from a topic list. The systems administrator trains people in person. Attendance is a {CALENDAR} entry plus a short list. The session is not replaced by a page.
tasks.previous_blocker: Practice sheets were rewritten for each class, and attendance lived in a notebook that nobody else could read.
tasks.enabler_now: A topic list and a system id can fill a sheet, and a calendar can hold the class without a new tool.
tasks.still_hard: People learn by doing the task with a person present. A sheet does not correct a mistake in the room.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator trains the people and decides when a person is not ready.
tasks.altitude: The sheet takes less rewriting. The training stays with the administrator.

reach.task: Practice the computer system task after the class
reach.learn: Which topics were covered and which people have not yet attended

evidence.claim: Training people to use a computer system is a live session. A practice sheet can be prepared. The session cannot be skipped.
In a mid-size firm this is a room or a call with a small group, not a course catalogue. Attendance is a list, not a certificate.

assumptions: Focal role is the systems administrator. The task is training people in computer system use. Writing a full course is out of scope.
Input contract: topic id, system id, class date, person name. Producer of the topic list is the administrator. Producer of attendance is the class. A topic with no system id is not put on the sheet.
The session stays person to person. The calendar and the document store are configured before custom code. The sheet is reviewed before the class. No model speaks to the people in the room.
unknowns: Which topics have no stable system id.
Whether a works site wants the class in person or on a call.
Who trains people when the administrator is away.
research_questions: How many people repeat the same class?
Which topics generate a support question the same week?

already_counted.description: Administrator edits the practice sheet before the class
Training people stays with the administrator

incremental.description: Revise the sheet when a computer system screen changes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes topics are new each time, so the sheet is rewritten and the class is unchanged. The high case assumes a reusable sheet, while the training itself is not treated as saved. Attendance recording is the only other small saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Spend time attending seminars or taking classes
Research technologies by reading trade articles
Draft whether to recommend the technologies

loop.input: filed notes and the recommendation template
loop.output: a draft that cites source ids only
loop.check: Every cited source id is on a filed note
loop.stop: One pass, then drop any sentence with no source id
loop.why_not_simpler: Whether a technology fits the firm is not a summary of the article

steps.what: Recommend the implementation or refuse it
Implement the signed technologies change

tasks.design: The systems administrator still attends seminars and reads trade articles. A bounded note in {DOCS} drafts whether to recommend a technology, citing only the notes they filed. Implementation on a live system happens only after they sign, and they do it themselves.
tasks.previous_blocker: Seminar notes and articles were unordered, so a recommendation could not show which source it used.
tasks.enabler_now: A note can store a source id and a technology name that a recommendation can cite.
tasks.still_hard: Judging whether a technology fits this firm is not a summary of an article, and attending cannot be delegated.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator recommends or refuses the implementation, and performs any implementation they sign.

ambition.what: Review the technology shortlist twice a year, not only when a seminar happens to fall

tasks.altitude: Filing notes is lighter. Attending, reading and the decision stay with the administrator, who can refuse a technology.

reach.learn: Which technologies were recommended and which were refused

evidence.claim: Researching technologies by seminars, articles and classes is a person's time. A note can organise what they already read. It cannot attend for them.
Digest [S28] reports a coding agent that deleted a production database despite instructions, so implementing a new technology on a live system is not left unattended.

assumptions: Focal role is the systems administrator. The task covers research and either a recommendation or an implementation they perform. A full project to roll out the technology is out of scope.
Input contract: source id, technology name, date, note text. Producer is the administrator from the seminar or the article. A note with no source id is not cited.
Attending and reading stay manual. The document store is configured before custom code. The recommendation draft does not change a live system.
unknowns: Who else must agree before implementation.
Which technologies are already refused by policy.
research_questions: How many recommended technologies were implemented last year?
What share of notes has no source id?

already_counted.description: Reading and judging articles stays with the administrator

incremental.description: Keep the note template aligned when source types change

approvals.approved_version: technology decision signed in this review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes notes stay unordered, so the draft rarely cites a source and the work is unchanged. The high case assumes a cleaner recommendation, while attending, reading, the decision and any implementation stay manual. No unattended implementation is counted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Report voice equipment trouble
Provide technical support for voice services
Draft technical support for known voice faults

loop.output: a note that cites one runbook id
loop.check: The note cites a runbook id for that equipment symptom
loop.stop: If none matches, return an empty note and stop
loop.why_not_simpler: A new symptom phrase does not match the runbook by a fixed table

steps.what: Sign the private branch exchange change
Implement the signed telecom system change
Advise on telecom system equipment

tasks.design: Voice trouble arrives on a {HELPDESK} form with a site and an equipment id. A bounded note drafts technical support for a known fault. The systems administrator signs any private branch exchange change and implements it by hand. The vendor engineer advises on telecom equipment the firm does not own. The user conversation stays a person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Voice faults were phone calls with no equipment id, so a repeated fault on the exchange was diagnosed from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: A ticket can store an equipment id and a symptom that a short support note can key on.
tasks.still_hard: A live exchange change can drop calls, and some telecom faults belong to the vendor.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator provides the technical support and signs the exchange change.
tasks.altitude: Known voice faults take less gathering. The administrator still supports the user and can refuse a change.

reach.task: Advise on telecom equipment the firm does not own
reach.learn: Which exchange changes are signed and which faults are waiting on the vendor

evidence.claim: Voice support is a mix of a user call and a change on the exchange. The call stays. A known fault can start from a note.
Digest [S1] and [S2] say a service desk can suggest a ticket category and draft a knowledge item for a person to review.
Digest [S15] is a vendor self-service claim of fewer tickets, with no published baseline, so this design does not count fewer voice tickets as time saved.
Digest [S28] reports a coding agent that deleted a production database despite instructions, so an unattended change to the exchange is out of scope.

assumptions: Focal role is the systems administrator. The task is technical support for voice services and equipment, including the private branch exchange, voice mail and the telecom system.
Input contract: ticket id, equipment id, site, symptom, user. Producer is the system user. A ticket with no equipment id skips the draft.

The user conversation stays person to person. Native phone-system tools are configured before custom code. The meeting-heavy prior overstates workshops: much of the time is at the exchange and on the call.
unknowns: Which parts of the telecom system the vendor owns.
Who may change the exchange when the administrator is away.
Whether voice mail messages are in scope of a privacy review. This design does not read them.
research_questions: What share of voice faults repeats a known symptom?
How often does an exchange change get rolled back?

already_counted.description: The user support call stays with the administrator
Administrator reviews a weak support draft

incremental.description: Add voice symptoms to the runbook after repeated faults
Vendor time on telecom faults the firm does not own

approvals.approved_version: exchange change signed for this ticket id

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes tickets have no equipment id, so the note rarely fires and support stays fully manual. The high case assumes a useful note, while the call and every exchange change stay manual. No unattended change and no ticket-volume claim are counted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Load tapes and install software or forms

steps.what: Load computer tapes and disks by hand
Install printer paper or forms by hand
Sign the software install for this computer
Install the signed software on the computer
Record the forms and tapes just loaded

tasks.design: Loading computer tapes and disks, and installing printer paper or forms, stays a person at the machine. A {WORKFLOW} form lists software to install. The systems administrator signs that list and installs it by hand on the computer. A short record notes which forms and tapes were loaded. Nothing installs unattended.
tasks.previous_blocker: Software to install arrived as a verbal ask, and nobody recorded which tapes or forms were loaded.
tasks.enabler_now: A list can hold a software id and a computer id, so the signature cites that list rather than a conversation.
tasks.still_hard: Tapes, disks, paper and forms are physical. A job cannot load them.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator loads the media and signs which software to install.
tasks.altitude: The record of what was loaded is shorter. The loading and the software install stay with the administrator.

reach.task: Collect printed forms after they are loaded
reach.learn: Which software was signed for install and which tapes were loaded

evidence.claim: Loading tapes, disks, printer paper and forms is physical work at the machine. A mid-size firm still does it by hand. A software list is the only part that can be a form.
Digest [S28] reports a coding agent that deleted a production database despite instructions, so installing software on a live computer is not left unattended.

assumptions: Focal role is the systems administrator. The task is loading computer tapes and disks, and installing software and printer paper or forms.

Input contract: computer id, software id, media id, forms type, quantity. Producer of the software ask is the system user. Producer of the load is the administrator. A software row with no computer id is not signed.
The in-person prior fits the loading. It does not mean a meeting. Native install tools are used before custom code. The workflow prior overstates this task: paper and tapes cannot be a job.
unknowns: Which computers still accept tapes or disks.
Who loads forms at a site with no administrator on the day.
Whether a software install needs a change window.
research_questions: How many software installs are repeats of a signed list?
How often is the wrong form loaded?

already_counted.description: Loading tapes and disks stays with the administrator
Loading paper and forms stays with the administrator
The software install stays with the administrator

incremental.description: Add a software id when a new package is allowed

approvals.approved_version: software install version signed for this computer id
the same signed software install version

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes every install is a one-off verbal ask, so the list saves little and loading is unchanged. The high case assumes a signed software list, while loading tapes, disks, paper and forms, and the install itself, stay manual. No unattended install is counted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Training, research and physical loading stay with the administrator. Signed software installs and voice changes are the only narrowed queue.
reach: System users leave a class with a practice sheet and a date, not a link they were never shown.
The vendor engineer sees which telecom fault is signed before opening the exchange.
skills_to_grow: Keep a training session as a session, and prepare only the sheet.
Separate reading a technology from implementing it on a live system.
State a voice change as a version before anyone touches the exchange.
role.ambitious_version: Classes, seminars and tape loading stay human, and every live software or voice change has a signed version.
